reviews.title: Good but confusing to use
reviews.text:
I’ve had this app for a while now and I don’t know if it’s a me thing or just UI but it’s rather odd to use it. For example, when I press the “Start Focus” I’m expecting for me to be able to choose from the different types of focus timers that I have and that is why I don’t press the play button but doing that automatically starts with the default 25 minute timer as opposed to my custom one. 

Resuming a focus session also does not properly start when it needs to. 

I like the app but these items affect the user experience in my opinion and I can get used to just about any software.

reviews.title: How long are we gonna put up with this?
reviews.text:
First off, the pricing model is totally predatory. The only free trial is if you agree to be charged a whole year’s membership fee after the seven-day trial period.  There’s no free trial if you opt for just monthly payments. I wonder why that would be?  Also, how long are we going to tolerate apps asking you a bunch of irrelevant questions prior to even being able to test the app?  Can I please just test your service without feeling like I’m being herded?   

When I finally got to the app, I realized it was overly complicated and could not really do what I wanted it to do, which was track the amount of time I spend in specific habits by using timers for those activities.  Overall, I feel like I was charged $13 so that I could make the 30 second assessment that this app was not for me. This could have been avoided with a free trial.

reviews.title: Issue Summary
reviews.text:
Issue Summary:
I noticed a problem in how Focus Keeper calculates focus time during a Pomodoro cycle.
Today, I completed the first session normally. In the second session, I had 7 minutes left but had to stop and leave the app from morning until late at night. When I came back at night, I finished the remaining 7 minutes, then completed sessions 3 and 4.
My real focus time for the day was 100 minutes.
However, the Achievements page counted the long break (from morning to night) as if it were focus time, and showed more than 10 hours of focus.
Expected behavior: The app should count only the actual minutes spent focusing, even if a session is paused for many hours.
Actual behavior: When a session is paused for a long time, the app adds the entire real-world gap to the focus total, which makes the daily focus time incorrect.
Please fix this issue so the focus time reflects actual work time only.
